title: Roles in a Group
keyIdea: People in a group can do different jobs, called roles. The leader keeps the plan and gives out jobs. The ideas person thinks of new things to try. The supporter helps build and cheers others on. The peacemaker, or mediator, helps both sides be heard and find a fix. A group works best with a mix of roles, not with everyone trying to lead.

kid: A group is a team that works on one job. In a good group, each friend has a role. A role is the job you do in the group.

The leader keeps the plan. She says, “Floor first, then walls.” The ideas person says, “What if we add a ladder?” The supporter holds the plank and says, “Great job!” The peacemaker helps when friends do not agree. Another word for peacemaker is mediator.
What if all four friends want to lead? They all say, “My way!” Nobody builds, so nothing gets done. One leader is enough. The others pick a different job.

Every role counts. With no supporter, nobody holds the planks. With no peacemaker, a fight stops the work. You do not always have to be in charge. Some days you lead, and some days you help a friend’s idea.
adult: This lesson teaches the main roles children take in group work and why a group needs a mix of them. It sits in the Interactions strand of the IB PYP personal, social and physical education scope, and in the CASEL relationship skills of teamwork, collaborative problem-solving and showing leadership in groups. The PSHE Association programme of study for key stage 2 also asks pupils to work collaboratively and to resolve disagreements.

Key terms for ages 7 to 9: group, role, leader, ideas person (or idea-generator), supporter (sometimes called an encourager), peacemaker or mediator, take turns, compromise, and cooperate. Many classrooms use set cooperative-learning roles, such as facilitator, recorder, timekeeper and encourager. The names differ, but the idea is the same: each member has a clear job.

Common mistakes: thinking the leader is the most important person, so every child competes for it and the supporting jobs feel like losing. Thinking a mediator decides who is right, when a mediator helps both sides say what they want and then look for a fix both can accept. And thinking a role is fixed for life, rather than something a child can change from one task to the next.

In the lab your child hands out badges to four friends who all want to lead, until one leader is left and the treehouse is built. They match what friends say to each role, fix three stuck teams by adding the missing role, and take one role away at a time to see what breaks. Then they pick their own favourite role and read its strength and its watch-out. Every drag has a big button twin.

familyTip: Next time you cook or tidy up together, give out roles first: one leader who keeps the plan, one ideas person, one helper and one peacemaker. Swap roles next time, then ask your child which role felt best and why.

visual.caption: Which role is this friend doing? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: Thinks of a new way to fix it
Helps two friends find a fix

lab.caption: Flagship lab: hand out badges to a team of leaders, match roles, add the missing one, and see what breaks without each.

practice.prompt: Leo says, “What if we make the den into a pirate ship?” Which role is Leo doing?
practice.hint: Is Leo making a plan, thinking of something new, helping, or calming an argument?
practice.explain: A pirate ship is a new thing to try, so Leo is the ideas person. A peacemaker helps friends who do not agree.

practice.prompt: A team has {n} friends. Only 1 friend is the leader. How many friends do other jobs?
practice.hint: Take the 1 leader away from the {n} friends.
practice.explain: {n} take away 1 is {=n-1}. Those {=n-1} friends can be the ideas person, supporters or the peacemaker.

practice.prompt: Ava and Ben both want to go first and start to shout. What does a peacemaker do?
choices: Help each one say what they want, then find a fix
Tell them both to go away
practice.hint: A peacemaker, or mediator, does not pick a winner.
practice.explain: The peacemaker helps both sides be heard, then helps them find a fix, like taking turns. Picking Ava as the winner is not mediating.

practice.prompt: A team needs 4 roles: leader, ideas person, supporter and peacemaker. {n} of the roles have someone. How many roles still need someone?
practice.hint: Start with 4 roles and take away the {n} that are done.
practice.explain: 4 take away {n} is {=4-n}. The team should find someone for each empty role so no job is missed.

pool.prompt: What is a role in a group?
choices: The job you do in the group
pool.hint: Think of the badges in the lab: crown, light bulb, helping hands and dove.
pool.explain: A role is your job in the group, like leader, ideas person, supporter or peacemaker.

pool.prompt: Four friends all want to be the leader. What will most likely happen?
choices: They argue, and little gets done
pool.hint: Think of the treehouse when every friend said “My way!”
pool.explain: Four leaders give four different orders, so nobody builds. One leader is enough, and the others do other jobs.

pool.prompt: Jo holds the box steady and says, “Well done!” Which role is Jo doing?
pool.hint: Who helps build and cheers the others on?
pool.explain: Helping and cheering is the supporter’s job. The supporter makes the plan real.

pool.prompt: Kai says, “First we get the paper, then we cut. Sam, you hold the glue.” Which role is that?
pool.hint: Who makes the plan and gives out the jobs?
pool.explain: Making the plan and giving out jobs is what a leader does.

pool.prompt: Is a supporter less important than the leader?
choices: No, the group needs every role
pool.hint: What happened in the lab when the supporter sat out?
pool.explain: No. Without a supporter, nobody holds the planks and nothing gets built. Every role counts.

pool.prompt: Your group picks Mia’s idea, not yours. What helps the group most?
choices: Stop helping until they pick yours
Keep saying your idea is better
pool.hint: You do not always have to be in charge, or have your idea win.
pool.explain: Helping with the chosen idea is a real job: you are being a supporter. Pushing your idea again stops the work.

pool.prompt: {n} friends all want to lead. Only 1 can be the leader. How many friends need to pick a different role?
pool.hint: One friend leads. Count the rest.
pool.explain: {n} take away the 1 leader is {=n-1}. Those {=n-1} friends can do ideas, help or keep the peace.

pool.prompt: A team has a leader, a supporter and a peacemaker, but they cannot think what to make. Which role is missing?
pool.hint: They are stuck for something new to try. Who thinks of new things?
pool.explain: The ideas person is missing. When a group is stuck, ask which job nobody is doing.

pool.prompt: There are {n} groups in a class. Each group has 1 peacemaker. How many peacemakers are there?
pool.hint: Count 1 peacemaker for each of the {n} groups.
pool.explain: 1 peacemaker in each of {n} groups makes {=n} peacemakers, so every group has someone to help when friends disagree.
